diagnosis.root_cause: The OLT health check is internally inconsistent and is reporting the OLT as healthy despite seven of eight tested PONs being marked failed. The live probe also shows every ONU on the in-scope EPON0/7 port definitively offline, indicating a real PON-port outage beneath the defective health-status logic.
evidence: The OLT responds to ping, SNMP, and the OID subtree, and its CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime are within healthy ranges; this is not an OLT failure.
The OLT health record says overall_status is healthy while seven of eight tested PONs are listed as failed, which is a contradictory summary/detail result.
The rules identify a healthy label hiding failures on all or all but one tested PON as a monitoring health-check defect.
The live ONU probe responds for every ONU on EPON0/7 with online:0 and auth state Una uth/MPCP DEREG; responds:true with online:0 is a definite offline result, not a monitoring silence.
All probed ONUs on the in-scope port are offline, so the service impact is a whole PON-port outage rather than a single ONU or splitter boundary.
The OLT remains reachable while its ONUs are definite negatives, which indicates failed PON-port service rather than a failed OLT.

Historical optical telemetry was stable and normal: RX stayed around -21 dBm, TX around +2.3 dBm, distance remained 166, and TX bias remained healthy. There is no evidence of fibre, laser, or distance degradation causing the current outage.

RADIUS records, line ID mapping, the expected VLAN 1047, router heartbeat, and recent traffic/session state are consistent, so authentication, VLAN provisioning, router reachability, and session flapping are not the cause.

remediation.action: Correct the OLT health-check status aggregation so failed PON details cannot produce an overall healthy result. Immediately investigate and restore EPON0/7 as a PON-port outage, including port hardware, uplink/feeder, and splitter checks. Do not classify this as an OLT-wide failure because ping, SNMP, and the OLT subtree respond normally. Verify ONU recovery and clear the alarm after the port is operational.

ground_truth.root_cause: The health check marks an OLT critical only when every sampled PON fails. Seven of eight failed here, so it wrote 'healthy' with a null error description while healthy_pons stood at 1 of 8 in the same record. A genuine multi-port outage is running underneath a healthy verdict.
expected_reasoning: The health record reports overall_status healthy with a null error description
The same record holds healthy_pons 1 against total_pons_tested 8, and seven entries in failed_pons_list
The summary label contradicts the detail fields inside one record
The check sets critical only when every sampled PON fails, so seven of eight yields healthy by design
Probing confirms every ONU on EPON0/7 returns responds true with online 0, a definite negative
oid_subtree_responds is true, so this is not the firmware mismatch mechanism
43 of 272 customers on the OLT are offline, far above the 4.85% background rate
Sessions ended together and PON traffic has collapsed from 219 to 6 Mbps
This is a genuine multi-port outage that the health check's status rule conceals

expected_escalation.review_reason: The health check reported healthy during a seven-port outage; the status rule needs correcting

distractors: The health record says healthy, inviting a no_fault conclusion
A scheduled scan with no complaint gives no reason to look harder
The fault type is a health check defect but the service impact is real
